verdict.headline: US-Canada tariff war erupts as Nvidia earnings week and Warsh Jackson Hole debut begin
verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — 0 of 3 regime triggers breached: Brent $93.09 (below $94 gate; breach resolved but Canada 50% tariffs live and Bessent Iran sanctions press conference 18:00 GMT). 30Y 5.25% (5bps from gate). BTC $77,502 above $62K floor. Event density this week is highest of the year: NVDA AH Aug 26 + GDP/PCE Wed-Fri + Warsh Jackson Hole Fri.
verdict.horizon: through Aug 28 (Warsh Jackson Hole keynote + PCE as week-end clearing events)
verdict.rationale_short: Brent pulled back to $93.09 at the Monday open — 130 cents below Friday's formal $94 trigger breach — as oil traders sold ahead of Bessent's 18:00 GMT Iran sanctions press conference (classic buy-the-rumor, sell-the-news unwind). The Brent regime breach is resolved; formal trigger count drops to 0 of 3. The step-aside posture shifts from oil-driven to calendar- and tariff-driven. US-Canada trade talks collapsed Friday night, triggering 50% tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods effective immediately with Canada retaliating dollar-for-dollar; automotive supply chains, energy transport, and consumer goods pricing are all in the blast radius. S&P 500 futures are off 0.3% premarket and Nasdaq futures down 0.5%; DXY firms 0.21% to 98.94 on risk-off. The week's event stack is dense: NVDA earnings AH Wednesday (consensus $93-95B revenue, ~96% YoY growth; Vera Rubin platform timeline commentary as key forward signal), Q2 GDP 2nd estimate and Personal Income/Spending both Wednesday morning, Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote Friday (1-in-3 September rate-hike odds; topic 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy'), and PCE Friday. The Canada tariff shock is the overlooked new risk: 50% levies with matching Canadian retaliation compound structural inflation from oil still above $90/bbl — exactly the environment Warsh will need to acknowledge on Friday. BTC at $77,502 live (Crypto.com; +0.91% 24h) remains pinned below the $80K ceiling with no Clarity Act Senate floor date. Step aside until Bessent's Iran announcement and the NVDA print clear the event queue.

trade_setups.asset: NVDA — binary event AH August 26; do not pre-position
trade_setups.thesis: NVDA's own Q2 FY27 guide is $91B revenue (±2%) and non-GAAP GM ~75%; Q1 actual was 78.4%, making the 75% guide a company-set floor. Street consensus has risen to $93-95B revenue (~96% YoY growth), implying the buy-side is already above the company's guide. The two-factor bar to drive a positive re-rating: (1) data-center revenue materially above the implied ~$77-79B consensus range, AND (2) non-GAAP GM at or above 76-77% (not just the 75% company floor). Vera Rubin platform transition timeline commentary is the new forward-looking watch: any pull-forward of Vera Rubin production ramp or expansion of the inference architecture addressable market sets the next multiple. The event stack context: GDP prints Wednesday morning before the open (Q2 2nd estimate; soft GDP + NVDA beat = best-case risk-on), Warsh keynote Friday (two days after the print with no de-risk gap). Canada tariff/supply chain context: NVDA's direct Canada revenue is limited, but secondary rare-earth risk from Beijing (rejected diplomacy last week) is the tail on supply.
trade_setups.entry: ~$219 current. $225 is resistance. $205 is the defined-risk stop entering post-print. AMD two closes above $484 before Aug 26 are the pre-event leading indicator — AMD has not achieved this.
trade_setups.invalidation: AMD fails $484 before Aug 26 AND NVDA GM prints at or below 75% (company's own floor); or Bessent's Iran sanctions produce a Brent reversal above $96 before Wednesday, activating stagflation overlay on the NVDA print night.
trade_setups.horizon: AH Aug 26 result; Warsh Jackson Hole Aug 28 is the immediate post-print macro risk event.

trade_setups.asset: Oil — 'sell the news' on Bessent Iran press conference 18:00 GMT
trade_setups.thesis: Brent has already sold off 1.38% to $93.09 in anticipation of Bessent's 18:00 GMT press conference, pulling the formal regime breach back below $94. If the announced sanctions match the 'toughest-ever' rhetoric (secondary sanctions on Chinese buyers), oil's initial reaction is likely to be a further squeeze before sellers reassert demand-destruction pricing. The structural dynamic: secondary sanctions on China (the marginal buyer of Iranian crude) are simultaneously a supply shock AND a demand shock for Chinese import demand of global crude — a self-limiting mechanism. Short-term, the 'buy the rumor' has already run; 'sell the news' continuation targets $91-92 Brent in the 24-48 hours post-announcement unless sanctions are materially more aggressive than priced.
trade_setups.entry: Brent ~$93.09 heading into 18:00 GMT. $91-92 target on 'sell the news' reaction. $94 re-entry above the trigger is the stop/reversal signal — a close above $94 post-announcement reactivates the regime breach.
trade_setups.invalidation: Sanctions details include direct military asset targeting or Strait of Hormuz closure threat not previously flagged; or Beijing announces immediate retaliatory export controls on rare earths (re-activates the commodity shock overlay).

trade_setups.asset: MRNA / XLV healthcare — structural rotation destination
trade_setups.thesis: MRNA's Phase 3 melanoma success is the first mRNA cancer vaccine at this endpoint. The mechanism shifts XLV from defensive-rotation to structural-catalyst status: there is now a confirmed, large-sample efficacy dataset in one of oncology's hardest endpoints. The sector-rotation logic is particularly valid in a week where tech faces binary NVDA risk, macro is uncertain, and the Canada tariff shock pressures broad industrials. XLV provides diversified healthcare exposure without single-name binary risk. MRK (Keytruda combination partner) is the lowest-volatility access point.
trade_setups.entry: XLV for diversified exposure. MRNA: monitor for consolidation post-gap before re-entry. MRK for lower-volatility combination-partner exposure.
trade_setups.invalidation: FDA raises manufacturing or safety concerns; broad market selloff on NVDA miss or Warsh hawkish surprise overrides the sector-specific catalyst.
trade_setups.horizon: 4-8 weeks; FDA submission timeline and investor day as the next catalysts.

bear_case: The US-Canada tariff shock is the new inflationary input that the August 23 verdict did not price: 50% tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods (effective immediately) alongside dollar-for-dollar Canadian retaliation create a structural cost-push inflation input that arrives simultaneously with oil still above $90/bbl and the 30Y only 5bps from its formal gate. The sequence that gets materially worse: Bessent's 18:00 GMT press conference announces secondary sanctions more aggressive than priced (e.g. direct asset-freeze of Chinese state oil companies, not just purchase restrictions), oil reverses the morning's sell-off and closes above $94 — reactivating the Brent regime breach and triggering the stagflation framework for the second consecutive session. Simultaneously, Canada's Carney announces retaliatory action targeting US tech and financial services (not just goods), expanding the trade war beyond the initially flagged $20B in goods. NVDA prints Wednesday AH with non-GAAP GM at or below 75% (company's own floor, below Q1 actual of 78.4%) — signaling the AI infrastructure buildout is decelerating faster than the buy-side modeled. In that sequence, Wednesday's GDP 2nd estimate prints soft (below 2.0%), and Warsh on Friday signals the hiking cycle is not finished — 'structural inflation from tariffs is not transitory' — repricing September hike odds from 1-in-3 to near-even. The 30Y breaks 5.30% for the first time this cycle. Multiple regime triggers activate simultaneously for the first time. The S&P 500 corrects sharply from the 7,650 premarket level toward 7,400-7,500. The breadth of the downside catalyst list — tariffs, Iran sanctions, NVDA binary, rate path, and GDP in a 72-hour window — is why the step-aside posture is maintained even with 0 formal triggers active today.
